channel.title: The PHP Dictionary — Recent Changes
channel.description: Recently added or updated entries in the PHP Dictionary.

item.title: Base Conversion
item.description: Base conversion turns an integer written in one numeric base into the same value written in another base.

item.title: Offline Test Suite
item.description: An offline test suite is a set of tests that run without network access.

item.title: Malformed Response Body
item.description: A malformed response body is an HTTP response whose content does not match what the client expects.

item.title: Least Privilege Principle
item.description: The principle of least privilege states that every user, process, service, or component should be granted only the minimum rights it needs to perform its task, and nothing more, for the minimum time needed.

item.title: Canned Response
item.description: A canned response is a fixed, pre-recorded answer that a test returns instead of calling the real service.

item.title: Code Duplication
item.description: Code duplication happens when the same, or nearly the same, block of code is written more than once in a project.

item.title: Constructor Property Promotion
item.description: Constructor property promotion lets a class declare its properties directly in the constructor signature.

item.title: Contract Test
item.description: A contract test checks that two sides of an interface agree on the messages they exchange.

item.title: array_change_key_case()
item.description: ``array_change_key_case()`` is a native PHP function that returns a copy of an array where all the string keys are converted to lowercase or uppercase.

item.title: End of Life (EOL)
item.description: End of life, or EOL, is the date after which a software version no longer receives updates, including security fixes.

item.title: End of Line (EOL)
item.description: End of line, or EOL, is the character or sequence of characters that marks the end of a line of text in a file.

item.title: Security
item.description: Security involves implementing measures and best practices to protect the application and its data from malicious attacks and vulnerabilities.

item.title: Template
item.description: A template is a preset document, filled with values in placeholders, to display the resulting data.

item.title: Markup
item.description: Markup is a way to write text with annotations that describe its structure or its presentation.

item.title: GPU Computing
item.description: GPU computing, or general-purpose computing on graphics processing units, uses the many parallel cores of a graphics card to run calculations that are not about drawing images.

item.title: Self-Hosted
item.description: Self-hosted means running an application or service on infrastructure that you control, rather than using a version run by someone else.

item.title: Authorization Header
item.description: The Authorization header carries the credentials that a client sends to a server to authenticate a request.

item.title: WeakReference
item.description: ``WeakReference`` is a final class that holds a reference to an object without keeping that object alive.

item.title: Database
item.description: A database is an organized set of data, which may be queried.

item.title: Extract, Transform, Load (ETL)
item.description: ETL, for Extract, Transform, Load, is a three-stage process used to move data from one or more source systems into a target system.

item.title: Monitoring
item.description: Monitoring is the process of observing, tracking, and analyzing the performance, health, and behavior of applications or infrastructure over time.

item.title: Types Erasure
item.description: Type Erasure is the removal of type annotations from the source code when going to production.

item.title: Type Parametricity
item.description: Type parametricity, or parametric polymorphism, is the ability to write a function, class, or interface once and have it work uniformly over any type, with that type supplied as a parameter rather than hard-coded.

item.title: Erased Types
item.description: Erased types are type parameters or annotations that exist while the code is analysed or compiled, and are gone when the program runs.

item.title: Flat File
item.description: A flat file is a plain, unstructured file that stores data as text or binary, with no indexes, relations or query engine of its own.

item.title: Broken Object Level Authorization (BOLA)
item.description: Object Level Authorization is a mechanism that checks if a user has the right to access or execute an action on a specific object.

item.title: Canary Token
item.description: A canary token is a fake credential, file, URL or record, planted where an attacker is likely to find it.

item.title: Canary Test
item.description: A canary test is a deliberately trivial test that is expected to pass.

item.title: Data Lakehouse
item.description: A data lakehouse combines the low-cost, open storage of a data lake with the management features of a data warehouse.

item.title: Data Warehouse
item.description: A data warehouse is a database built for analysis rather than for running an application.

item.title: Data Lake
item.description: A data lake is a storage repository that keeps large volumes of data in its raw, original format until it is needed.

item.title: PHP_VERSION_ID
item.description: ``PHP_VERSION_ID`` is a predefined integer constant holding the version of the running PHP interpreter, encoded as ``major * 10000 + minor * 100 + release``.

item.title: version_compare()
item.description: ``version_compare()`` compares two version strings, and is the correct way to compare PHP or library versions.

item.title: Reified Types
item.description: Reified types are generic type parameters that are kept at runtime, so the code can check or create the actual type argument while the program runs.

item.title: Generics
item.description: Generics, sometimes called ``parametered polymorphism``, or more precisely parametric polymorphism, are a style of types, where the type of a property, parameter or return is specified at the declaration level.

item.title: Software Bill Of Material (SBOM)
item.description: A Software Bill of Materials, aka ``SBOM``, is a formal, machine-readable inventory of all components, libraries, and dependencies used in a software project.

item.title: __halt_compiler()
item.description: ``__halt_compiler()`` halts the execution of the compiler.

item.title: __sleep() Method
item.description: ``__sleep()`` is called when an object is being serialized, so that the object may be prepared before storage.

item.title: Abstract Keyword
item.description: PHP has ``abstract`` classes, properties and methods.

item.title: And Operator
item.description: ``and`` is the logical operator of the same name.

item.title: Anonymous Catch
item.description: Traditionally, the catch statement requires specifying both an Exception class and an identifier variable to hold the caught exception.

item.title: Ahead Of Time
item.description: Ahead-of-time compilation, ``AOT``, is the process of compiling source code to machine code before execution, as opposed to at runtime.

item.title: Application Programming Interface (API)
item.description: An API is a set of functions and procedures allowing the creation of applications that access the features or data of another service.

item.title: Argon2
item.description: Argon2 is a modern, secure, and highly efficient password hashing algorithm.

item.title: Array, []
item.description: ``array`` is the array structure.

item.title: array_map()
item.description: ``array_map()`` is a PHP native function that applies a closure to every element of an array.

item.title: Arrow Functions
item.description: Arrow functions, introduced with the ``fn`` keyword, are a type of closure with a specific syntax.

item.title: Artifact
item.description: An artifact refers to any intermediate or final output that is produced during the development process.

item.title: As
item.description: The as operator has several usages:

item.title: Bearer Token
item.description: A bearer token is an access credential sent with an HTTP request to prove the caller's identity.
